title: Summer News Notes 08.10.26
textContent:
Section 1
In a loving, nurturing environment, St. Martha School guides each student to develop his or her unique ability and potential through prayer, study and service.

[1] TMARTHAJ
PARISH & SCHOOL [ig

26-27 Calendar: Important Upcoming Dates
August 11 - New Family Night 5:00pm August 20 - Meet the Miracles & Supply Drop-Off August 24 - First Day of School (Half Day): August 24, 25, 26 Kindergarten: Half Days September 9 - 4 YO Preschoolers begin September 10 - 3 YO Preschoolers begin There is always the possibility of a change throughout the school year.

26-27 Academic Calendar - Subject to Change
Please review the calendar for updates made in July.
26-27 Academic Calendar (9).pdf

New Family Orientation - Tuesday, August 11
Join us for an informative evening to help your family get comfortable, learn key school procedures, and kick off a successful school year! When: Tuesday, August 11, 2026 at 5:00 PM Where: Blessed Solanus Casey Conference Room (Use school Door 2 to enter the building) What to Expect: School Overview: Schedules, arrival/dismissal, safety, and care programs. Office & Resources: FACTS portal, lunch ordering, uniforms, and health procedures. Get Involved: volunteering, athletics, and school events. Guided Campus Tour: Classrooms, gym, church, library, playground, and more! Live Q&A: Get all your last-minute questions answered. We can’t wait to meet you and welcome you into our school community!
New Family Orientation - RSVP

Meet the Miracles
St. Martha Catholic School is excited to welcome all families, new and veteran to Meet the Miracles ! This special event is a wonderful opportunity for current families, new families, teachers, and staff to come together, mix and mingle, and celebrate the beginning of a new school year. We are especially excited to welcome our many new families joining us across Preschool–8th Grade and look forward to helping them feel at home in our St. Martha community. Meet the Miracles will take place on Thursday, August 20th from 5:30-7pm at the St. Martha Playground Area . Families can enjoy hot dogs, chips, lemonade, and cookies. Feel free to bring a blanket or chairs if you would like a place to sit and visit. Fr. Ryan, Mrs. Konopaska, and the St. Martha teachers and staff will be there and are looking forward to welcoming everyone! An RSVP is not required, but it is helpful for planning purposes. Please click the link below if you plan (or hope) to attend:
Meet the Miracles RSVP & Volunteer Sign UP

FACTS update information from the Diocese of Lansing
Please log in to the FACTS Family Portal as soon as possible to ensure you are able to access and navigate the site following their recent summer update. Updated District Code: Please note that our district code has changed from STMS-MI to LANSING-DIO . Handbooks: Once logged in, you can view copies of our Student Handbook and Technology Handbook. Medication Permission Form: The "Permissions for Meds" form is also available on FACTS. If your child needs to take any medication at school, including over-the-counter medicine, this form must be completed and on file before we can accept or administer any medication. Allergies or Medical Conditions: If your child has experienced any changes regarding medical conditions or allergies since enrollment, please let me know immediately so we can keep their records up to date. Criminal Background Check Form: Available on FACTS. If it has been more than five years since your last background check, please print out this form and return it with your summer packet. You can review your status at any time by logging into VIRTUS.org . Please begin using the updated Family Portal link: https://sis. factsmgt .com/ family-portal?DistrictCode= LANSING-DIO If you previously bookmarked the old Family Portal, please update your bookmark. District Code: LANSING-DIO Sign In Sign in using your existing email address/username and password.

26-27 District Code Update:
Please use: LANSING-DIO
in place of STMS-MI
We encourage all families to try logging in to FACTS this
week. If you cannot login, please email Mrs. Farnsworth. If
you receive and error, please send a screenshot.

Summer Packets
If you do not receive your packet by tomorrow, please contact Mrs. Farnsworth at: cfarnsworth@st-martha.org Packets returned to the school may be picked up by appointment only.

Important Checklist for Preschool, Kindergarten, 7th Grade & New Families
To ensure your child is ready to start school on August 24th , please make sure the following documents are submitted: Health Appraisal Immunization Records (or an official county waiver) Birth Certificate (New families) Note on Immunizations: If your child’s appointment is scheduled for after the start of the school year, please provide a copy of your appointment card for our records. Please enclose all documents in your summer packet envelope

Important Update: New School Lunch Ordering Process
Starting this school year, Lansing Catholic will transition to monthly lunch ordering rather than daily orders. Ordering Deadline: Lunch orders must be placed on FACTS one week before the new month begins. Full instructions on how to order through FACTS will be included in your summer packet. Absences: If your student is sick or absent, their lunch order for that day will be removed and will not be charged. Emergency Meals: If a student forgets their lunch, we can add a last-minute order. Please note that this option is for emergencies only and cannot be used on a regular basis.

Staff Wish Lists
As we kick off the new school year, families often ask if there are extra supplies or items our classrooms could use. If you’re ever interested in checking out what’s on a teacher’s classroom wish list, we’ve gathered everything in one handy spot! Please click below to view the lists. Here’s to a great year ahead!
School Office
Mrs. Belloli - Preschool
Mrs. Lamke - Kindergarten
Mrs. Ramereiz - First Grade
Miss Marth - Second Grade
Mrs. Plaehn (Jacobs) - Third Grade
Mrs. Plefka - Fourth Grade
Miss Flint - Fifth Grade
Mr. Quintus - Sixth Grade
Mrs. Hall - Seventh Grade
Mrs. Richardson - Eighth Grade
Mrs. Welte - Student Advocate
Mrs. Ardis - Strings
Mrs. Muzzatti - Technology

Teacher
© Staff

Supply List
Supply lists are here! If you have any specific questions about supplies or what to bring, please reach out directly to your child's homeroom teacher.
PS-2nd Grade Supply List
Supply List PS-2.pdf
3rd-8th Grade Supply List
Supply List 3-8.pdf

Uniform Information
Maroon polos are now in stock! This optional new addition to our uniform is available for grades K–8 and can be worn with skirts, pants, or shorts. (Please note: Jumpers still require the Peter Pan collar blouse.) If you have any questions reqgarding our uniform, please contact me as soon as possible. We ask that families please take time to review all pages carefully, paying special attention to the shoe guidelines. To help ensure consistency with our dress code expectations, please do not send students to school wearing shoes listed in the “No” category , including Sambas, Converse, Nike Low Dunks, and high-top styles. Socks should be crew style without branding. Please avoid no show, or other low-cut sock styles. Shoes can be black or grey only . No additional colors on the shoes including logos. If you have any questions regarding the guidelines, please feel free to reach out. We appreciate your support and partnership in helping our students follow the Uniform and Dress Code expectations. Free shipping on order $50 and up. Use code: FREESHIP14
Uniform Guidelines
My APlus Uniforms

AVAILABLE
*

Spirit Wear is Back!
Our St. Martha School Spirit Wear Shop through Fabricated Customs is back! The shop will now remain open indefinitely , making it easy to grab your favorite gear anytime during the year. From cozy sweatshirts and stylish tees to fun options for both kids and adults , there’s something for everyone to show their St. Martha School pride!
Fabricated Customs - Spirit Wear

textContent:
Section 1

A Message from Mrs. Konopaska
I hope you are enjoying a wonderful summer! It has been a busy and productive one here at St. Martha as construction continues to move forward. While we are excited about the progress, the project has brought about changes to timelines and plans. As a result, some details may continue to evolve as we prepare for the start of the school year. Please know that our students are always at the heart of every decision. I will continue to advocate for the best opportunities and learning environment for each child. As we begin the new school year, I ask for your grace, patience, and flexibility as we navigate any unexpected changes together. Change isn't always easy, but I am confident that, as a school community, we will work through it together. It is an honor to serve St. Martha. I am grateful for the opportunity to partner with our families, support our dedicated staff, and help our students grow academically, spiritually, and personally. Thank you for your continued trust and support. I look forward to welcoming everyone back soon! - Mrs. Konopaska

Important Note
Mrs. Konopaska is out of the office July 31st- August 10th and will return and emails or calls when she returns.

The building will remain closed until Friday, July 31. Masses on Wednesday, July 29 and Thursday, July 30 will take place outside the narthex door (north entrance) of the church building. Adoration on Wednesday and confessions both Wednesday and Thursday are cancelled.

St. Martha Catholic School is excited to welcome all families, new and veteran to Meet the Miracles ! This special event is a wonderful opportunity for current families, new families, teachers, and staff to come together, mix and mingle, and celebrate the beginning of a new school year. We are especially excited to welcome our many new families joining us across Preschool–8th Grade and look forward to helping them feel at home in our St. Martha community. Meet the Miracles will take place on Thursday, August 20th from 5:30-7pm at the St. Martha Playground Area . Families can enjoy hot dogs, chips, lemonade, and cookies. Feel free to bring a blanket or chairs if you would like a place to sit and visit. Fr. Ryan, Mrs. Konopaska, and the St. Martha teachers and staff will be there and are looking forward to welcoming everyone! An RSVP is not required, but it is helpful for planning purposes. Please click the link below if you plan (or hope) to attend:
Meet the Miracles RSVP & Volunteer Sign UP

FACTS update information from the Diocese of Lansing
We’re pleased to let you know that the FACTS system update for the Diocese of Lansing has been successfully completed. Thank you for your patience throughout this transition. By bringing all diocesan schools together under a single district in FACTS , we have created a more consistent experience for families while improving communication, reporting, and administration across the Diocese—all while maintaining your student records and tuition information . What You Need to Do Access the New Family Portal Please begin using the updated Family Portal link: https://sis. factsmgt .com/ family-portal?DistrictCode= LANSING-DIO If you previously bookmarked the old Family Portal, please update your bookmark. Sign In Sign in using your existing email address/username and password. If prompted, follow the on-screen instructions to verify your account or reset your password. Verify Your Information After signing in, please take a moment to confirm that: All of your students appear in your account. Student information is accurate. Enrollment and tuition information appear as expected. If you notice anything that doesn't look correct—such as a missing student, duplicate record, or other issue—please contact your school office so we can assist you. Online Payments Online payments through the Family Portal are now available again. You may resume making payments online as usual. Any previously scheduled automatic payments will continue without interruption. Thank you again for your patience and partnership throughout this transition. We appreciate your support as we continue enhancing the experience for families across the Diocese of Lansing.

26-27 District Code Update:
Please use: LANSING-DIO
in place of STMS-MI
We encourage all families to try logging in to FACTS this
week. If you cannot login, please email Mrs. Farnsworth. If
you receive and error, please send a screenshot.

Summer Packets
Summer packets will be mailed August 4th. If you do not receive your packet, please contact Mrs. Farnsworth at: cfarnsworth@st-martha.org If you have recently updated your address, please update your information on FACTS before the end of the week. Packets returned to the school may be picked up by appointment only.

Important Update: New School Lunch Ordering Process
Starting this school year, Lansing Catholic will transition to monthly lunch ordering rather than daily orders. Ordering Deadline: Lunch orders must be placed on FACTS one week before the new month begins. Full instructions on how to order through FACTS will be included in your summer packet. Absences: If your student is sick or absent, their lunch order for that day will be removed and will not be charged. Emergency Meals: If a student forgets their lunch, we can add a last-minute order. Please note that this option is for emergencies only and cannot be used on a regular basis.

Acceptable Use Policy for Electronic Devices Chromebooks, and Technology
Please review our updated Acceptable Use Policy for Electronic Devices Chromebooks, and Technology. You will receive a form to sign in our summer packet. Coming soon: Parent & Student Handbook

Supply List
Supply lists are here! If you have any specific questions about supplies or what to bring, please reach out directly to your child's homeroom teacher.
PS-2nd Grade Supply List
Supply List PS-2.pdf
3rd-8th Grade Supply List
Supply List 3-8.pdf

Maroon short sleeve polo shirts will be available as a new option for the 26-27 school year for K-8. Since this is a new additional option to our uniform collection, there will be some lead time before maroon polos are available for our school. Once they are available, they will be added to the website and I will notify families. This will only be available in short sleeves. Free shipping on order $50 and up. Use code: FREESHIP14

Section 11
I want to express my deepest gratitude to our staff, students, and families for the incredible love and kindness you have shown me as I prepare to retire. The cards, gifts, thoughtful notes, prayers, celebrations, and countless acts of generosity have touched my heart more than words can express. Each gesture has been a reminder of the special community we have built together and the many blessings God has poured upon our school. To our students, thank you for filling my days with joy, laughter, curiosity, and hope. Watching you learn, grow, and deepen your faith has been one of the greatest privileges of my life. To our parents and families, thank you for your trust, partnership, support, and friendship throughout the years. It has been an honor to work alongside you in nurturing the minds, hearts, and souls of your children. To our dedicated staff, thank you for your unwavering commitment, your compassion, and your shared mission of serving God's children. The friendships, memories, and experiences we have shared will remain among my greatest treasures. To our parish community, thank you for your ongoing prayers, encouragement, and generosity toward our school. The partnership between parish and school is a true blessing, building a strong foundation of faith for our students and families. It has been a privilege to serve in a community that lives the Gospel so fully and values the formation of young people in both faith and learning. I will always cherish being part of a parish family that so deeply supports Catholic education. To Fr. Ryan, Fr. Mike, and the deacons, thank you for the gift of your priesthood, your ministry, and your friendship. You have walked alongside our school community in times of joy and challenge, always pointing us toward God’s presence among us. Your kindness, wisdom, and faithful witness have been a personal blessing to me, and I am deeply grateful for the opportunity to have served with you. As I reflect on my years here, my heart is full of gratitude. While retirement brings a new adventure, I will always carry this school and all of you with me. I have been blessed beyond measure by the relationships we have formed and the faith we have shared. Thank you for making this transition so meaningful and for honoring me in such thoughtful ways. Your kindness has been a gift I will never forget. May God continue to bless each of you and our school community. Please know that you will always remain in my prayers. With heartfelt gratitude and love, Andrea Patton

Section 2
As we enter severe weather season, we would like to remind families of our emergency safety procedures. If the school receives a severe weather or emergency alert requiring us to shelter in place, our protocol is to keep all students safely inside the building until the alert has been lifted by emergency officials. We understand that delays during dismissal and pick-up times can be inconvenient and stressful for families. However, the safety and well-being of our students and staff must remain our top priority, even if it means students remain at school longer than usual. Once students are safely sheltered, we are unable to release students individually, send them back to classrooms to gather belongings, or coordinate staggered dismissals during the emergency. Doing so creates disruption at a time when staff members are focused on maintaining a safe and orderly environment for all students. Families will receive updates and notifications through email and text communication as information becomes available and when normal dismissal procedures may resume. Thank you for your understanding, cooperation, and support as we work together to keep our students safe.

A Message from Mrs. Konopaska
St. Martha Families- As I begin in the role of principal for the 26–27 school year, I want to say how grateful I am for the foundation that has already been built and for the care and commitment families bring to our school community. Parents are the first and primary educators of their children, and the school’s work is strengthened when we truly partner together. This partnership also calls us to communicate openly and collaborate toward shared educational goals. With that in mind, I would like to invite you to a Meet & Greet with me . These gatherings are a chance for us to connect, share, and build relationships. I’m especially looking forward to listening, learning, and understanding what’s working well and what matters most to you, so we can continue to grow together. Please attend on whichever date is most convenient: Tuesday, June 2 at 8:30-9:30am AND 3:30-4:30pm Please wait to enter the building until 8:25am and drop off students using our normal carline procedures In addition, I would be grateful if you could complete a brief survey to help shape our plans for the 26–27 school year. textSections.heading: Section 2
textSections.text:
As we enter severe weather season, we would like to remind families of our emergency safety procedures. If the school receives a severe weather or emergency alert requiring us to shelter in place, our protocol is to keep all students safely inside the building until the alert has been lifted by emergency officials. We understand that delays during dismissal and pick-up times can be inconvenient and stressful for families. However, the safety and well-being of our students and staff must remain our top priority, even if it means students remain at school longer than usual. Once students are safely sheltered, we are unable to release students individually, send them back to classrooms to gather belongings, or coordinate staggered dismissals during the emergency. Doing so creates disruption at a time when staff members are focused on maintaining a safe and orderly environment for all students. Families will receive updates and notifications through email and text communication as information becomes available and when normal dismissal procedures may resume. Thank you for your understanding, cooperation, and support as we work together to keep our students safe.

textSections.heading: Construction Updates
textSections.text: We have trucks on-site and the dirt is moving! We are excited to see this next phase of construction underway. A few important reminders to ensure everyone’s safety: Please do not enter or walk near the construction area at any time. Students should not climb on the fence or go beyond the fence into the construction area. Parking on the west side of the building is prohibited. Please use designated parking areas only. textSections.heading: A Message from Mrs. Konopaska
textSections.text:
St. Martha Families- As I begin in the role of principal for the 26–27 school year, I want to say how grateful I am for the foundation that has already been built and for the care and commitment families bring to our school community. Parents are the first and primary educators of their children, and the school’s work is strengthened when we truly partner together. This partnership also calls us to communicate openly and collaborate toward shared educational goals. With that in mind, I would like to invite you to a Meet & Greet with me . These gatherings are a chance for us to connect, share, and build relationships. I’m especially looking forward to listening, learning, and understanding what’s working well and what matters most to you, so we can continue to grow together. Please attend on whichever date is most convenient: Tuesday, June 2 at 8:30-9:30am AND 3:30-4:30pm Please wait to enter the building until 8:25am and drop off students using our normal carline procedures In addition, I would be grateful if you could complete a brief survey to help shape our plans for the 26–27 school year. All families are encouraged to participate as your input is valued as we move into the next school year. Thank you in advance for your time and trust. I look forward to meeting you and working together. Survey deadline: Friday, May 22nd

As we enter severe weather season, we would like to remind families of our emergency safety procedures. If the school receives a severe weather or emergency alert requiring us to shelter in place, our protocol is to keep all students safely inside the building until the alert has been lifted by emergency officials. We understand that delays during dismissal and pick-up times can be inconvenient and stressful for families. However, the safety and well-being of our students and staff must remain our top priority, even if it means students remain at school longer than usual. Once students are safely sheltered, we are unable to release students individually, send them back to classrooms to gather belongings, or coordinate staggered dismissals during the emergency. Doing so creates disruption at a time when staff members are focused on maintaining a safe and orderly environment for all students. Families will receive updates and notifications through email and text communication as information becomes available and when normal dismissal procedures may resume. Thank you for your understanding, cooperation, and support as we work together to keep our students safe.

Construction Updates
We have trucks on-site and the dirt is moving! We are excited to see this next phase of construction underway. A few important reminders to ensure everyone’s safety: Please do not enter or walk near the construction area at any time. Students should not climb on the fence or go beyond the fence into the construction area. Parking on the west side of the building is prohibited. Please use designated parking areas only. Be alert in the parking lot, as there will be increased truck traffic throughout the day. Follow all posted signs and any temporary traffic pattern changes. Thank you for your cooperation as we work through this exciting time while keeping safety our top priority.

A Message from Mrs. Konopaska
St. Martha Families- As I begin in the role of principal for the 26–27 school year, I want to say how grateful I am for the foundation that has already been built and for the care and commitment families bring to our school community. Parents are the first and primary educators of their children, and the school’s work is strengthened when we truly partner together. This partnership also calls us to communicate openly and collaborate toward shared educational goals. With that in mind, I would like to invite you to a Meet & Greet with me . These gatherings are a chance for us to connect, share, and build relationships. I’m especially looking forward to listening, learning, and understanding what’s working well and what matters most to you, so we can continue to grow together. Please attend on whichever date is most convenient: Monday, May 18th, 3:30pm-4:30pm Friday, June 2, 8am-9am In addition, I would be grateful if you could complete a brief survey to help shape our plans for the 26–27 school year. All families are encouraged to participate as your input is valued as we move into the next school year. Thank you in advance for your time and trust. I look forward to meeting you and working together. Survey deadline: Friday, May 22nd

textSections.heading: Construction Updates
textSections.text: We have trucks on-site and the dirt is moving! We are excited to see this next phase of construction underway. A few important reminders to ensure everyone’s safety: Please do not enter or walk near the construction area at any time. Students should not climb on the fence or go beyond the fence into the construction area. Parking on the west side of the building is prohibited. Please use designated parking areas only. Be alert in the parking lot, as there will be increased truck traffic throughout the day. Follow all posted signs and any temporary traffic pattern changes. Thank you for your cooperation as we work through this exciting time while keeping safety our top priority.

textSections.heading: A Message from Mrs. Konopaska
textSections.text:
St. Martha Families- As I begin in the role of principal for the 26–27 school year, I want to say how grateful I am for the foundation that has already been built and for the care and commitment families bring to our school community. Parents are the first and primary educators of their children, and the school’s work is strengthened when we truly partner together. This partnership also calls us to communicate openly and collaborate toward shared educational goals. With that in mind, I would like to invite you to a Meet & Greet with me . These gatherings are a chance for us to connect, share, and build relationships. I’m especially looking forward to listening, learning, and understanding what’s working well and what matters most to you, so we can continue to grow together. Please attend on whichever date is most convenient: Monday, May 18th, 3:30pm-4:30pm Friday, June 2, 8am-9am In addition, I would be grateful if you could complete a brief survey to help shape our plans for the 26–27 school year. All families are encouraged to participate as your input is valued as we move into the next school year. Thank you in advance for your time and trust. I look forward to meeting you and working together. Survey deadline: Friday, May 22nd

textSections.heading: Maria Goretti Scholarship
textSections.text: St. Martha Parish and School are seeking ten individual donors who can make a four-year commitment to provide $100 a year to sponsor an eighth grader to attend Lansing Catholic High School. The ten individual donations combined will provide for one $1000 St. Maria Goretti Scholarship, to be awarded at 8th grade graduation, renewable each year the student attends Lansing Catholic High School. The student is chosen by the St. Martha School staff for his/her conduct, grades, overall Christian behavior and display of virtues expected at a Catholic School. We have been fortunate to award this scholarship to several students throughout the years and we would like to continue the tradition. Please contact the Parish office (517-349-1763) as soon as possible if you are able to financially assist a young student with their Catholic Education.

Construction Updates
We have trucks on-site and the dirt is moving! We are excited to see this next phase of construction underway. A few important reminders to ensure everyone’s safety: Please do not enter or walk near the construction area at any time. Students should not climb on the fence or go beyond the fence into the construction area. Parking on the west side of the building is prohibited. Please use designated parking areas only. Be alert in the parking lot, as there will be increased truck traffic throughout the day. Follow all posted signs and any temporary traffic pattern changes. Thank you for your cooperation as we work through this exciting time while keeping safety our top priority.

A Message from Mrs. Konopaska
St. Martha Families- As I begin in the role of principal for the 26–27 school year, I want to say how grateful I am for the foundation that has already been built and for the care and commitment families bring to our school community. Parents are the first and primary educators of their children, and the school’s work is strengthened when we truly partner together. This partnership also calls us to communicate openly and collaborate toward shared educational goals. With that in mind, I would like to invite you to a Meet & Greet with me . These gatherings are a chance for us to connect, share, and build relationships. I’m especially looking forward to listening, learning, and understanding what’s working well and what matters most to you, so we can continue to grow together. Please attend on whichever date is most convenient: Monday, May 18th, 3:30pm-4:30pm Friday, June 2, 8am-9am In addition, I would be grateful if you could complete a brief survey to help shape our plans for the 26–27 school year. All families are encouraged to participate as your input is valued as we move into the next school year. Thank you in advance for your time and trust. I look forward to meeting you and working together. Survey deadline: Friday, May 22nd

Maria Goretti Scholarship
St. Martha Parish and School are seeking ten individual donors who can make a four-year commitment to provide $100 a year to sponsor an eighth grader to attend Lansing Catholic High School. The ten individual donations combined will provide for one $1000 St. Maria Goretti Scholarship, to be awarded at 8th grade graduation, renewable each year the student attends Lansing Catholic High School. The student is chosen by the St. Martha School staff for his/her conduct, grades, overall Christian behavior and display of virtues expected at a Catholic School. We have been fortunate to award this scholarship to several students throughout the years and we would like to continue the tradition. Please contact the Parish office (517-349-1763) as soon as possible if you are able to financially assist a young student with their Catholic Education.

Attention 26-27 Kindergarten Families!
We are excited to welcome our preschool friends who are enrolled in our Kindergarten program for the 2026–2027 school year! Join us for a special Kindergarten Orientation designed to help both parents and students feel confident and ready for this exciting next step. Date: May 12 Time: 6:00 PM Location: Mrs. Lamke's Classroom - Room 112 For Parents: Mrs. Lamke will share important information about what to expect in kindergarten and how you can help your child prepare for a successful start to the school year. For Students: Mrs. Belloli, along with our wonderful teacher aides, will spend time with the children in the classroom. Students will enjoy fun activities, meet new friends, and begin getting comfortable in their new environment. This is a great opportunity to ease the transition into kindergarten and build excitement for the year ahead! We look forward to seeing you there and beginning this journey together

textSections.heading: Construction Updates
textSections.text: We have trucks on-site and the dirt is moving! We are excited to see this next phase of construction underway. A few important reminders to ensure everyone’s safety: Please do not enter or walk near the construction area at any time. Students should not climb on the fence or go beyond the fence into the construction area. Parking on the west side of the building is prohibited. Please use designated parking areas only. Be alert in the parking lot, as there will be increased truck traffic throughout the day. Follow all posted signs and any temporary traffic pattern changes. Thank you for your cooperation as we work through this exciting time while keeping safety our top priority.

textSections.heading: A Message from Mrs. Konopaska
textSections.text:
St. Martha Families- As I begin in the role of principal for the 26–27 school year, I want to say how grateful I am for the foundation that has already been built and for the care and commitment families bring to our school community. Parents are the first and primary educators of their children, and the school’s work is strengthened when we truly partner together. This partnership also calls us to communicate openly and collaborate toward shared educational goals. With that in mind, I would like to invite you to a Meet & Greet with me . These gatherings are a chance for us to connect, share, and build relationships. I’m especially looking forward to listening, learning, and understanding what’s working well and what matters most to you, so we can continue to grow together. Please attend on whichever date is most convenient: Monday, May 18th, 3:30pm-4:30pm Friday, June 2, 8am-9am In addition, I would be grateful if you could complete a brief survey to help shape our plans for the 26–27 school year. All families are encouraged to participate as your input is valued as we move into the next school year. Thank you in advance for your time and trust. I look forward to meeting you and working together. Survey deadline: Friday, May 22nd
26-27 School Survey

textSections.heading: The BOOK FAIR is BACK!!! We need your help!
textSections.text:
Join us for our Ignatius Book Fair! This is a wonderful opportunity to explore inspiring, faith-filled books for all ages. From stories of the saints to engaging reads for young learners, there’s something for everyone to enjoy. Come discover books that strengthen faith, spark curiosity, and encourage a love of reading. It’s also a great way to support our school while finding meaningful resources for your family. We’ve partnered with Ignatius Book Fairs to bring a great selection of inspiring books and fun, faith-based trinkets for everyone to enjoy! The fair will run May 11–17. Please check your calendars and see if you’re available to help with setup or assist with sales during the week. textSections.heading: Maria Goretti Scholarship
textSections.text: St. Martha Parish and School are seeking ten individual donors who can make a four-year commitment to provide $100 a year to sponsor an eighth grader to attend Lansing Catholic High School. The ten individual donations combined will provide for one $1000 St. Maria Goretti Scholarship, to be awarded at 8th grade graduation, renewable each year the student attends Lansing Catholic High School. The student is chosen by the St. Martha School staff for his/her conduct, grades, overall Christian behavior and display of virtues expected at a Catholic School. We have been fortunate to award this scholarship to several students throughout the years and we would like to continue the tradition. Please contact the Parish office (517-349-1763) as soon as possible if you are able to financially assist a young student with their Catholic Education.

textSections.heading: Attention 26-27 Kindergarten Families!
textSections.text: We are excited to welcome our preschool friends who are enrolled in our Kindergarten program for the 2026–2027 school year! Join us for a special Kindergarten Orientation designed to help both parents and students feel confident and ready for this exciting next step. Date: May 12 Time: 6:00 PM Location: Mrs. Lamke's Classroom - Room 112 For Parents: Mrs. Lamke will share important information about what to expect in kindergarten and how you can help your child prepare for a successful start to the school year. For Students: Mrs. Belloli, along with our wonderful teacher aides, will spend time with the children in the classroom. Students will enjoy fun activities, meet new friends, and begin getting comfortable in their new environment. This is a great opportunity to ease the transition into kindergarten and build excitement for the year ahead! We look forward to seeing you there and beginning this journey together

Lansing Catholic High School offers Jr. Cougar programming for those in grades K-8 . https://lansingcatholic.org/jrcougars Since 22-23, Jr. Cougars compete in with the Capital Athletic Association Conference (CAAC) for 7th & 8th grade sports in Cross-Country, Volleyball, Basketball (Girls & Boys), and Track. Several of our spring sports registrations are now OPEN! At this link (and found below), you’ll find registration information for: Youth Soccer - Grades K–3 Baseball - U8, U10, U12, U14 Softball - U8, U10, U12, U14 Track & Field - Grades 6-8 Tennis - Ages 14 & Under If we fail to have enough participants at a certain age level, we will work on an alternative placement in collaboration with what works best for your individual needs! Details will be coming for our youth lacrosse programs as we align with the transitions our high school is making this spring. St. Martha Parish and School are seeking ten individual donors who can make a four-year commitment to provide $100 a year to sponsor an eighth grader to attend Lansing Catholic High School. The ten individual donations combined will provide for one $1000 St. Maria Goretti Scholarship, to be awarded at 8th grade graduation, renewable each year the student attends Lansing Catholic High School. The student is chosen by the St. Martha School staff for his/her conduct, grades, overall Christian behavior and display of virtues expected at a Catholic School. We have been fortunate to award this scholarship to several students throughout the years and we would like to continue the tradition. Please contact the Parish office (517-349-1763) as soon as possible if you are able to financially assist a young student with their Catholic Education.

Attention 26-27 Kindergarten Families!
We are excited to welcome our preschool friends who are enrolled in our Kindergarten program for the 2026–2027 school year! Join us for a special Kindergarten Orientation designed to help both parents and students feel confident and ready for this exciting next step. Date: May 12 Time: 6:00 PM Location: Mrs. Lamke's Classroom - Room 112 For Parents: Mrs. Lamke will share important information about what to expect in kindergarten and how you can help your child prepare for a successful start to the school year. For Students: Mrs. Belloli, along with our wonderful teacher aides, will spend time with the children in the classroom. Students will enjoy fun activities, meet new friends, and begin getting comfortable in their new environment. This is a great opportunity to ease the transition into kindergarten and build excitement for the year ahead! We look forward to seeing you there and beginning this journey together

Non-Uniform Day Dress Guidelines
On non-uniform days, students are expected to dress in modest, school-appropriate clothing. Shorts should be an appropriate length; the fingertip rule is a helpful guideline. Tank tops, crop tops, and spaghetti (thin) strap tops are not permitted. Footwear should be modest, secure, and comfortable; flip-flops, and loose-fitting sandals are not allowed. All out-of-uniform attire should align with the expectations outlined in our school handbook.

Safety Drills
We will be conducting required safety drills in the coming weeks, including fire, tornado, and lockdown drills. These drills will be unannounced to both staff and students, as this helps us practice responding in a more realistic and effective way. Teachers review procedures with students ahead of time in a general and age-appropriate manner. You may also want to take a moment at home to talk with your child about the importance of these drills and reassure them that they are designed to help keep everyone safe .

The student is chosen by the St. Martha School staff for his/her conduct, grades, overall Christian behavior and display of virtues expected at a Catholic School. We have been fortunate to award this scholarship to several students throughout the years and we would like to continue the tradition. Please contact the Parish office (517-349-1763) as soon as possible if you are able to financially assist a young student with their Catholic Education.

textSections.heading: Non-Uniform Day Dress Guidelines
textSections.text: On non-uniform days, students are expected to dress in modest, school-appropriate clothing. Shorts should be an appropriate length; the fingertip rule is a helpful guideline. Tank tops, crop tops, and spaghetti (thin) strap tops are not permitted. Footwear should be modest, secure, and comfortable; flip-flops, and loose-fitting sandals are not allowed. All out-of-uniform attire should align with the expectations outlined in our school handbook.

textSections.heading: Safety Drills
textSections.text: We will be conducting required safety drills in the coming weeks, including fire, tornado, and lockdown drills. These drills will be unannounced to both staff and students, as this helps us practice responding in a more realistic and effective way. Teachers review procedures with students ahead of time in a general and age-appropriate manner. You may also want to take a moment at home to talk with your child about the importance of these drills and reassure them that they are designed to help keep everyone safe .

Lansing Catholic High School offers Jr. Cougar programming for those in grades K-8 . https://lansingcatholic.org/jrcougars Since 22-23, Jr. Cougars compete in with the Capital Athletic Association Conference (CAAC) for 7th & 8th grade sports in Cross-Country, Volleyball, Basketball (Girls & Boys), and Track. It’s a wonderful chance to make lasting memories, celebrate these special bonds, and enjoy a fun night together. We encourage all of our girls to join us for this special event!

Our date was set prior to their announcement, and while we would love for all of our girls to attend the St. Martha Daddy Daughter Dance, we understand that students may have other special events they wish to attend. textSections.heading: Non-Uniform Day Dress Guidelines
textSections.text: On non-uniform days, students are expected to dress in modest, school-appropriate clothing. Shorts should be an appropriate length; the fingertip rule is a helpful guideline. Tank tops, crop tops, and spaghetti (thin) strap tops are not permitted. Footwear should be modest, secure, and comfortable; flip-flops, and loose-fitting sandals are not allowed. All out-of-uniform attire should align with the expectations outlined in our school handbook.

textSections.heading: Safety Drills
textSections.text: We will be conducting required safety drills in the coming weeks, including fire, tornado, and lockdown drills. These drills will be unannounced to both staff and students, as this helps us practice responding in a more realistic and effective way. Teachers review procedures with students ahead of time in a general and age-appropriate manner. You may also want to take a moment at home to talk with your child about the importance of these drills and reassure them that they are designed to help keep everyone safe .

What is your favorite subject and why? Literature is my personal favorite. Literature and classical authors have always interested me. What is your favorite school tradition? My favorite school tradition is the Fish Fry. It is a great way to connect with your school friends outside of academics. What sports/extracurricular activities do you participate in? I have a couple different extracurricular activities that I do, but my personal favorites are Mathclub and soccer. What is you favorite book and why? I don't have a designated favorite book but I've always liked the ones with myths tied into the storyline. What is your favorite movie or TV show? I do not watch TV enough to have a favorite show. What is your favorite memory from St. Martha School? My favorite memory/memories was when I went to Suttons Bay for a field trip. What will you miss most about St. Martha School? I will miss the friendly atmosphere and teachers, along with the way that the small classes bring us together. What is your favorite thing to do when you have free time? I love to read in my free time. If you could visit any country where would you go and why? I would love to visit France to see the Eiffel tower or Japan to see the Shibuya crosswalk. What have you learned about yourself this year? I have learned that persistence always pays off even if it isn't in the way you expected. What high school are you attending next year? I will be attending Lansing Catholic. What are you most excited about for high school? I am really excited to see what House I will be in and how the Rodzinkas will work. What college do you want to attend? I would love to go to Michigan State. What is your dream job and why? If money didn't matter, I would take a job in the creative field, but right now I'm planning to pursue a job in the field of law. What is something that you’ve done that you are proud of? I am proud of myself for the growth I have seen in my mathematical abilities even if it isn't my favorite subject.

It is with great joy that we share some wonderful news! Mrs. Amanda Konopaska has graciously accepted our offer to serve as the next principal of St. Martha School. Mrs. Konopaska is a faithful leader with a wealth of experience, and she is truly excited to join the St. Martha team and we are just as excited to have her on board. We are very excited about the future of St. Martha School and look forward to all that lies ahead!

textSections.text: We are excited to welcome our preschool friends who are enrolled in our Kindergarten program for the 2026–2027 school year! Join us for a special Kindergarten Orientation designed to help both parents and students feel confident and ready for this exciting next step. Date: May 12 Time: 6:00 PM Location: Mrs. Lamke's Classroom - Room 112 For Parents: Mrs. Lamke will share important information about what to expect in kindergarten and how you can help your child prepare for a successful start to the school year. For Students: Mrs. Belloli, along with our wonderful teacher aides, will spend time with the children in the classroom. Students will enjoy fun activities, meet new friends, and begin getting comfortable in their new environment. This is a great opportunity to ease the transition into kindergarten and build excitement for the year ahead! We look forward to seeing you there and beginning this journey together

textSections.heading: Spring Uniforms
textSections.text:
Beginning in April 13, students may transition back into the summer uniform, including shorts! We recommend getting those shorts out now and having your child try them on. Not only have we seen tremendous academic growth this year, but our students seem to be growing taller by the day as well! If new items are needed, please place your order with My APlus as soon as possible so you are prepared when the warmer weather arrives. Thank you for your continued support! A couple of reminders: Skirts and jumpers should be no shorter than 2 inches above the knee Privacy shorts worn underneath cannot be longer than the hem of the skirts and jumpers and must be black, gray or navy only. Please ensure that student uniforms are in good condition and free from holes or permanent stains. Students K-4 may wear My A+ Navy shorts with their polo shirts. Students in 5-8 may wear My A+ Grey Shorts with their polo shirts.
My APlus Uniforms

textSections.heading: Section 12
textSections.text: My A+ is now online only and no longer has storefronts in Michigan. We will continue to use My A+, and all items will now ship from Tulsa. If you are having trouble placing an order, please contact Mrs. Farnsworth for assistance. We kindly ask that families avoid purchasing off-brand uniform pieces in place of those from My A+. Using the approved uniform items helps ensure consistency across all students and supports a unified appearance for our school community. We understand that the shift to online ordering may not be ideal for everyone, but we are not making any changes in uniform providers. This allows us to maintain a clear and consistent standard, especially now that there are no local uniform storefront options. We appreciate your understanding and cooperation.

textSections.heading: Safety Drills
textSections.text: We will be conducting required safety drills in the coming weeks, including fire, tornado, and lockdown drills. These drills will be unannounced to both staff and students, as this helps us practice responding in a more realistic and effective way. Teachers review procedures with students ahead of time in a general and age-appropriate manner. You may also want to take a moment at home to talk with your child about the importance of these drills and reassure them that they are designed to help keep everyone safe .

Camp Sancta Maria (located in Gaylord, MI) has spent 90 years helping young people grow closer to Jesus Christ through daily sacraments, authentic discipleship, adventure activities, and the beauty of God’s creation. An Eagle Scout project is a significant, community-oriented effort that demonstrates a Scout’s ability to plan, develop, and lead others while benefiting a school, church, or community organization. From start to finish, Drew led this project with dedication, selecting the idea, gaining approval, fundraising, and executing the build. We are incredibly grateful for the time, talent, and treasure Drew shared with our community. The kids LOVE it! What is your favorite subject and why? My favorite subject is math. Math is my favorite subject because to me it is kind of like a puzzle. I like how math is very black and white and seems to come naturally to me. Thinking logically is also what led me to join the Mathcounts team. Finally, my math teachers at my time at St. Martha have always been willing to help me grasp things I don't understand or push me further forward if I needed it. What is your favorite school tradition? There are a lot of school traditions I enjoy doing but one of my favorites is the end of the year class field trip. This is my favorite because it is a lot of fun to hang out with your classmates outside of school and the teachers always make them a lot of fun. My favorite end of the year fields trips so far have been Michigan Adventure and Sutton's Bay. I am also really excited for going to Mackinac Island this year. What sports/extracurricular activities do you participate in? I have been doing gymnastics since I was 3 years old. In the past I have tried different sports but always came back to gymnastics. When I moved to Michigan 5 years ago, my coach put me on the competitive team. I started as a Level 3 and I am currently competing as a Level 7. Competitive gymnastics is a year round sport so it is hard to participate in other sports or activities but I love to when I can! What is you favorite book and why? I have many favorite books so it is hard to pick exactly one. The genre I lean towards is fantasy. I think that fantasy can throw you into an alternative dimension and lets your mind escape reality. What is your favorite movie or TV show? My favorite movies are the Harry Potter movies. What is your favorite memory from St. Martha School? I have made a lot of memories that I am going to cherish forever at St. Martha School. One of my favorite though was in fourth grade. We were once all really tired in religion class so my teacher, Mrs. Lorencen, got out glycerin. She poured a little on each of our desks and we just made bubbles the whole class. Another one of my favorite memories happened last year. We were in Sutton's Bay and our whole class played volleyball on the beach while we watch the sun set. It was really fun to hang out as a whole class and feel so connected. What will you miss most about St. Martha School? The thing I will miss most about St. Martha School is the teachers and staff. The teachers at St. Martha are so kind, are always willing to help me out whenever I need, and are easy to talk to. I'll also miss it when Mr. Quintus would take us outside and we would just run laps around the school. The staff are also super nice and I will miss waving to Mr. Alchin in the hallway. What is your favorite thing to do when you have free time? When I am not in school or doing gymnastics one of my favorite things is to hang out with my family or supporting my siblings. If you could visit any country where would you go and why? I would like to visit France. I would like to go to France to see the Eiffel tower and eat French delicacies. What have you learned about yourself this year? This year I have learned about my self that I can learn things at a faster pace. This year my teachers have starting preparing us for high school and we have been working really hard. I found out that, even though its harder, I'm able to work a lot more than I thought I was able to. What high school are you attending next year? Next year I will be attending Lansing Catholic High School. What are you most excited about for high school? I am most excited for meeting new people and hopefully making new friends along the way. I am also excited for being able to try new things, join new clubs, and pick electives of things I've never done before. What college do you want to attend? I would like to get a scholarship for college but I think right now I would prefer to go to MSU. What is your dream job and why? I think what I want to lean towards when I'm older is something in the math or science field. What is something that you’ve done that you are proud of? Something that I have done that I'm proud of is that I have accomplished top scorer in school in Mathcounts two years in a row.

What is your favorite subject and why? My favorite subject is math. Math is my favorite subject because to me it is kind of like a puzzle. I like how math is very black and white and seems to come naturally to me. Thinking logically is also what led me to join the Mathcounts team. Finally, my math teachers at my time at St. Martha have always been willing to help me grasp things I don't understand or push me further forward if I needed it. What is your favorite school tradition? There are a lot of school traditions I enjoy doing but one of my favorites is the end of the year class field trip. This is my favorite because it is a lot of fun to hang out with your classmates outside of school and the teachers always make them a lot of fun. My favorite end of the year fields trips so far have been Michigan Adventure and Sutton's Bay. I am also really excited for going to Mackinac Island this year. What sports/extracurricular activities do you participate in? I have been doing gymnastics since I was 3 years old. In the past I have tried different sports but always came back to gymnastics. When I moved to Michigan 5 years ago, my coach put me on the competitive team. I started as a Level 3 and I am currently competing as a Level 7. Competitive gymnastics is a year round sport so it is hard to participate in other sports or activities but I love to when I can! What is you favorite book and why? I have many favorite books so it is hard to pick exactly one. The genre I lean towards is fantasy. I think that fantasy can throw you into an alternative dimension and lets your mind escape reality. What is your favorite movie or TV show? My favorite movies are the Harry Potter movies. What is your favorite memory from St. Martha School? I have made a lot of memories that I am going to cherish forever at St. Martha School. One of my favorite though was in fourth grade. We were once all really tired in religion class so my teacher, Mrs. Lorencen, got out glycerin. She poured a little on each of our desks and we just made bubbles the whole class. Another one of my favorite memories happened last year. We were in Sutton's Bay and our whole class played volleyball on the beach while we watch the sun set. It was really fun to hang out as a whole class and feel so connected. What will you miss most about St. Martha School? The thing I will miss most about St. Martha School is the teachers and staff. The teachers at St. Martha are so kind, are always willing to help me out whenever I need, and are easy to talk to. I'll also miss it when Mr. Quintus would take us outside and we would just run laps around the school. The staff are also super nice and I will miss waving to Mr. Alchin in the hallway. What is your favorite thing to do when you have free time? When I am not in school or doing gymnastics one of my favorite things is to hang out with my family or supporting my siblings. If you could visit any country where would you go and why? I would like to visit France. I would like to go to France to see the Eiffel tower and eat French delicacies. What have you learned about yourself this year? This year I have learned about my self that I can learn things at a faster pace. This year my teachers have starting preparing us for high school and we have been working really hard. I found out that, even though its harder, I'm able to work a lot more than I thought I was able to. What high school are you attending next year? Next year I will be attending Lansing Catholic High School. What are you most excited about for high school? I am most excited for meeting new people and hopefully making new friends along the way. I am also excited for being able to try new things, join new clubs, and pick electives of things I've never done before. What college do you want to attend? I would like to get a scholarship for college but I think right now I would prefer to go to MSU. What is your dream job and why? I think what I want to lean towards when I'm older is something in the math or science field. What is something that you’ve done that you are proud of? Something that I have done that I'm proud of is that I have accomplished top scorer in school in Mathcounts two years in a row.

Thank you for adjusting to our new drop-off and pick-up procedures. We truly appreciate your cooperation and support as we work to keep our students safe and ensure a smooth process for everyone. Please wait until 7:50 AM to exit vehicles to enter the building. The doors are locked prior to that time and will unlock promptly at 7:50 AM. Preschool Pick-Up (11:20 AM) Please wait by your vehicles for Mrs. Belloli to come outside for the 11:20 AM preschool pick-up. She will bring all of the children outside at the same time. The big playground is closed during school recess. We kindly ask that preschool families do not use the playground at that time so we can maintain safety and supervision for all students. Carline Option for Preschoolers If you are comfortable using the carline for drop-off with preschoolers who have older siblings, we have student helpers, along with Mrs. Patton and/or Mrs. Farnsworth, outside to assist children out of vehicles and to their classrooms if needed. Our 8th graders are eager to help and truly enjoy assisting our younger students! To help the carline move efficiently: Please make sure all K–8 students are ready to exit the vehicle and that goodbyes are said before pulling up. Pull forward as far as possible to the designated sign. For safety and efficiency, please do not let students out of vehicles far away from the building, as this slows the flow of traffic and prevents other cars from pulling forward. We kindly ask that everyone continue to be patient and drive carefully through the parking lot. Your attention and cooperation make a big difference in keeping our school community safe. Thank you again for your continued support.

What is your favorite subject and why? My favorite subject is English. I enjoy English because I love to read and write and Mrs. Richardson is an amazing teacher. What is your favorite school tradition? There is so many great traditions at St. Martha like the daddy daughter dance and fun day, but I think my favorite tradition is getting to free dress on your birthday. It makes your birthday feel a little more special and I always look forward to that. What sports/extracurricular activities do you participate in? Outside of school, I do singing lessons and have also participated in the Jr. Cougar Musicals for the last 3 years including Annie Jr., Mary Poppins Jr. and this years musical, Madagascar Jr. What is you favorite book and why? I love reading fantasy books. These kinds of books are my favorite because I love the magic and I also love the themes of good verse evil. One of my favorite series is The Land of Stories Series. What is your favorite movie or tv show? I love Wicked, the Harry Potter movies and many of the Marvel movies. I also love the Disney classics. What is your favorite memory from St. Martha School? I have many great memories at St. Martha. One that sticks out is from my first year at St. Martha when I was in 4th grade. I had to have a big surgery on my leg in New York City. Mrs. Lorencen and my classmates gave me a squishmellow before I left. They sent me videos while I was in the hospital and when I finally was able to return to school everyone, was very helpful and nice. My classmates argued over who got to push me around in my wheel chair! Some were better drivers than others! Mrs. Farnsworth was my most trusted driver. All of this made me feel very special. What will you miss most about St. Martha School? I will miss the teachers the most. They are best teachers I have ever had and I really appreciate all they have done for me. I will also miss being at school with my siblings and my Mom. What is your favorite thing to do when you have free time? My favorite thing to do in my free time is to watch movies or shows with my family. I also like to hang out with friends and I really have fun at my voice lessons . If you could visit any country where would you go and why? If I could visit any country it would probably be Italy. I would love to see the Vatican, the Pope, and eat lots of delicious Italian food. What have you learned about yourself this year? I have learned that I am stronger than I thought and with hard work I will persevere. What high school are you attending next year? I am very excited to attend Lansing Catholic High School. What are you most excited about for high school? I am excited to meet my new teachers, to meet new people and to make friends, and that some of my St. Martha friends will be there too. I am also excited for my classes and to participate in the musicals. What college do you want to attend? I like the idea of a small Christian school like Hope or Aquinas, but many of my family members went to Michigan State so I think that could be a good option also. What is your dream job? My dream job is something in music or acting. It would be fun and rewarding to teach music, and possibly continue to be involved in musicals. I also love animals, and think about becoming a veterinarian. What is something that you’ve done that you are proud of? I have had 5 surgeries in my life. Sometimes things feel hard, but I endured and learned how strong I am. This makes me feel proud. I am also proud of my grades at St. Martha. Not everything comes easy, but I work hard to get good grades.

Orton-Gillingham Training
Once again this year, the Granger Foundation has generously provided scholarship opportunities for our teachers to receive training in the Orton-Gillingham approach. Several teachers will be attending training over the next three Thursdays and Fridays. We are excited to share that, with this opportunity, our entire primary level will now be trained in this structured, multisensory method of teaching reading and providing reading intervention. We are grateful for the continued support of the Granger Foundation and look forward to the positive impact this training will have on our students.

Winter NWEA Results: Celebrating Student Growth (Grades 3-8)
We are excited to share that our Winter NWEA assessment data is in, and the results for St. Martha students are outstanding! Since our fall testing, we have seen significant academic growth across the board in both Reading and Math. Click here to see a graph and a table of percentile scores. Here is a quick guide to help you interpret these results: Beyond the Median: While the 50th percentile represents the national "average," St. Martha students scored in the upper-average to high-average range. Solid Proficiency: These scores indicate that our students are performing at and frequently above grade-level proficiency. National Excellence: Our school remains on a strong trajectory, performing exceptionally well when compared to national norms. The Power of Progress At St. Martha, we place a high value on individual growth. While raw scores naturally rise as students learn new concepts, these percentiles show that our students are not just keeping pace. they are making meaningful gains. We are incredibly proud of the hard work our students and teachers have put in this semester. Partnering for Success: How to Help at Home To keep this momentum going through the spring, here are a few simple ways you can support your child's continued growth: Discuss the Goals: Review the report with your child. The Mid-Michigan chapter of Graduate Women in Science (GWIS) would like to invite the students at your school to the 2026 Girls Math and Science Day at Michigan State University on Saturday, Mar 14th, 2026. This is a fantastic opportunity for middle school-aged students to participate in STEM demonstrations led by some of MSU's enthusiastic and knowledgeable students and researchers. This year, we want students to see and experience more types of STEM fields throughout the day, with the ability to revisit an activity as many times as they like. Therefore, the day for each participant will consist of two faculty talks, two 20-minute STEM-themed activities according to the student preference, a science fair-like session with a scavenger hunt, an afternoon snack, and an ice cream social with a gift bag giveaway and thank-you note signing. textSections.text:
Thank you for adjusting to our new drop-off and pick-up procedures. We truly appreciate your cooperation and support as we work to keep our students safe and ensure a smooth process for everyone. Please wait until 7:50 AM to exit vehicles to enter the building. The doors are locked prior to that time and will unlock promptly at 7:50 AM. Preschool Pick-Up (11:20 AM) Please wait by your vehicles for Mrs. Belloli to come outside for the 11:20 AM preschool pick-up. She will bring all of the children outside at the same time. The big playground is closed during school recess. We kindly ask that preschool families do not use the playground at that time so we can maintain safety and supervision for all students. Carline Option for Preschoolers If you are comfortable using the carline for drop-off with preschoolers who have older siblings, we have student helpers, along with Mrs. Patton and/or Mrs. Farnsworth, outside to assist children out of vehicles and to their classrooms if needed. Our 8th graders are eager to help and truly enjoy assisting our younger students! To help the carline move efficiently: Please make sure all K–8 students are ready to exit the vehicle and that goodbyes are said before pulling up. Pull forward as far as possible to the designated sign. For safety and efficiency, please do not let students out of vehicles far away from the building, as this slows the flow of traffic and prevents other cars from pulling forward. We kindly ask that everyone continue to be patient and drive carefully through the parking lot. Your attention and cooperation make a big difference in keeping our school community safe. Thank you again for your continued support.

textSections.heading: Section 10
textSections.text:
What is your favorite subject and why? My favorite subject is English. I enjoy English because I love to read and write and Mrs. Richardson is an amazing teacher. What is your favorite school tradition? There is so many great traditions at St. Martha like the daddy daughter dance and fun day, but I think my favorite tradition is getting to free dress on your birthday. It makes your birthday feel a little more special and I always look forward to that. What sports/extracurricular activities do you participate in? Outside of school, I do singing lessons and have also participated in the Jr. Cougar Musicals for the last 3 years including Annie Jr., Mary Poppins Jr. and this years musical, Madagascar Jr. What is you favorite book and why? I love reading fantasy books. These kinds of books are my favorite because I love the magic and I also love the themes of good verse evil. One of my favorite series is The Land of Stories Series. What is your favorite movie or tv show? I love Wicked, the Harry Potter movies and many of the Marvel movies. I also love the Disney classics. What is your favorite memory from St. Martha School? I have many great memories at St. Martha. One that sticks out is from my first year at St. Martha when I was in 4th grade. I had to have a big surgery on my leg in New York City. Mrs. Lorencen and my classmates gave me a squishmellow before I left. They sent me videos while I was in the hospital and when I finally was able to return to school everyone, was very helpful and nice. My classmates argued over who got to push me around in my wheel chair! Some were better drivers than others! Mrs. Farnsworth was my most trusted driver. All of this made me feel very special. What will you miss most about St. Martha School? I will miss the teachers the most. They are best teachers I have ever had and I really appreciate all they have done for me. I will also miss being at school with my siblings and my Mom. What is your favorite thing to do when you have free time? My favorite thing to do in my free time is to watch movies or shows with my family. I also like to hang out with friends and I really have fun at my voice lessons . If you could visit any country where would you go and why? If I could visit any country it would probably be Italy. I would love to see the Vatican, the Pope, and eat lots of delicious Italian food. What have you learned about yourself this year? I have learned that I am stronger than I thought and with hard work I will persevere. What high school are you attending next year? I am very excited to attend Lansing Catholic High School. What are you most excited about for high school? I am excited to meet my new teachers, to meet new people and to make friends, and that some of my St. Martha friends will be there too. I am also excited for my classes and to participate in the musicals. What college do you want to attend? I like the idea of a small Christian school like Hope or Aquinas, but many of my family members went to Michigan State so I think that could be a good option also. What is your dream job? My dream job is something in music or acting. It would be fun and rewarding to teach music, and possibly continue to be involved in musicals. I also love animals, and think about becoming a veterinarian. What is something that you’ve done that you are proud of? I have had 5 surgeries in my life. Sometimes things feel hard, but I endured and learned how strong I am. This makes me feel proud. I am also proud of my grades at St. Martha. Not everything comes easy, but I work hard to get good grades.

textSections.heading: Winter NWEA Results: Celebrating Student Growth (Grades 3-8)

Since our fall testing, we have seen significant academic growth across the board in both Reading and Math. Click here to see a graph and a table of percentile scores. Here is a quick guide to help you interpret these results: Beyond the Median: While the 50th percentile represents the national "average," St. Martha students scored in the upper-average to high-average range. Solid Proficiency: These scores indicate that our students are performing at and frequently above grade-level proficiency. National Excellence: Our school remains on a strong trajectory, performing exceptionally well when compared to national norms. The Power of Progress At St. Martha, we place a high value on individual growth. While raw scores naturally rise as students learn new concepts, these percentiles show that our students are not just keeping pace. they are making meaningful gains. We are incredibly proud of the hard work our students and teachers have put in this semester. Partnering for Success: How to Help at Home To keep this momentum going through the spring, here are a few simple ways you can support your child's continued growth: Discuss the Goals: Review the report with your child. textSections.heading: Girls Math & Science Day!
textSections.text:
The Mid-Michigan chapter of Graduate Women in Science (GWIS) would like to invite the students at your school to the 2026 Girls Math and Science Day at Michigan State University on Saturday, Mar 14th, 2026. This is a fantastic opportunity for middle school-aged students to participate in STEM demonstrations led by some of MSU's enthusiastic and knowledgeable students and researchers. Registration is FREE of cost and will be open from Feb 01st - 28th (or until spots are filled) ! This year, we want students to see and experience more types of STEM fields throughout the day, with the ability to revisit an activity as many times as they like. Therefore, the day for each participant will consist of two faculty talks, two 20-minute STEM-themed activities according to the student preference, a science fair-like session with a scavenger hunt, an afternoon snack, and an ice cream social with a gift bag giveaway and thank-you note signing. Students must register for the event using this link: https://forms.gle/Eguc9Dik8f29P8KYA
Pine Hills Boys & Girls Camp
Pine Hills Boys & Girls Camp is now preparing for its upcoming camp season, and registration opens March 1 . This popular camp is open to current 6th, 7th, and 8th graders , and spots are limited. Last year, the Girls Camp filled completely within one hour of registration opening , with many campers placed on a waitlist. Families interested in learning more about Pine Hills Camp or receiving registration information should reach out directly to Pine Hills or visit pinehillscamp .com. A “Save the Date” flyer with camp information is attached. Don’t miss the opportunity!

Spring Uniforms
Beginning in April, students may transition back into the summer uniform, including shorts! We recommend getting those shorts out now and having your child try them on. Not only have we seen tremendous academic growth this year, but our students seem to be growing taller by the day as well! If new items are needed, please place your order with My APlus as soon as possible so you are prepared when the warmer weather arrives. Thank you for your continued support!

Orton-Gillingham Training
Once again this year, the Granger Foundation has generously provided scholarship opportunities for our teachers to receive training in the Orton-Gillingham approach. Several teachers will be attending training over the next three Thursdays and Fridays. We are excited to share that, with this opportunity, our entire primary level will now be trained in this structured, multisensory method of teaching reading and providing reading intervention. We are grateful for the continued support of the Granger Foundation and look forward to the positive impact this training will have on our students.

Winter NWEA Results: Celebrating Student Growth (Grades 3-8)
We are excited to share that our Winter NWEA assessment data is in, and the results for St. Martha students are outstanding! Since our fall testing, we have seen significant academic growth across the board in both Reading and Math. Click here to see a graph and a table of percentile scores. Here is a quick guide to help you interpret these results: Beyond the Median: While the 50th percentile represents the national "average," St. Martha students scored in the upper-average to high-average range. Solid Proficiency: These scores indicate that our students are performing at and frequently above grade-level proficiency. National Excellence: Our school remains on a strong trajectory, performing exceptionally well when compared to national norms. The Power of Progress At St. Martha, we place a high value on individual growth. While raw scores naturally rise as students learn new concepts, these percentiles show that our students are not just keeping pace. they are making meaningful gains. We are incredibly proud of the hard work our students and teachers have put in this semester. Partnering for Success: How to Help at Home To keep this momentum going through the spring, here are a few simple ways you can support your child's continued growth: Discuss the Goals: Review the report with your child. Celebrate the progress they’ve made and ask them what they are excited to learn next. (Reports came home last week or at conferences) Reading Habits: Encourage 20 minutes of daily reading. Whether it’s a novel, a graphic novel, or an informational article, consistent exposure is key to maintaining those high reading percentiles. Math in the Real World: Help your child see math in action, whether it's calculating a tip, measuring ingredients for a recipe, or tracking sports statistics. IXL-Students in Grades 1-8 have access to IXL in school and at home where they can receive personalized practice and instruction in math and language arts. Thank you for your continued partnership in making St. Martha a place where academic excellence thrives!
