textSections.heading: Orton-Gillingham Training
textSections.text: Once again this year, the Granger Foundation has generously provided scholarship opportunities for our teachers to receive training in the Orton-Gillingham approach. Several teachers will be attending training over the next three Thursdays and Fridays. We are excited to share that, with this opportunity, our entire primary level will now be trained in this structured, multisensory method of teaching reading and providing reading intervention. We are grateful for the continued support of the Granger Foundation and look forward to the positive impact this training will have on our students.

textSections.heading: Winter NWEA Results: Celebrating Student Growth (Grades 3-8)
textSections.text:
We are excited to share that our Winter NWEA assessment data is in, and the results for St. Martha students are outstanding! Since our fall testing, we have seen significant academic growth across the board in both Reading and Math. Click here to see a graph and a table of percentile scores. Here is a quick guide to help you interpret these results: Beyond the Median: While the 50th percentile represents the national "average," St. Martha students scored in the upper-average to high-average range. Solid Proficiency: These scores indicate that our students are performing at and frequently above grade-level proficiency. National Excellence: Our school remains on a strong trajectory, performing exceptionally well when compared to national norms. The Power of Progress At St. Martha, we place a high value on individual growth. While raw scores naturally rise as students learn new concepts, these percentiles show that our students are not just keeping pace. they are making meaningful gains. We are incredibly proud of the hard work our students and teachers have put in this semester. Partnering for Success: How to Help at Home To keep this momentum going through the spring, here are a few simple ways you can support your child's continued growth: Discuss the Goals: Review the report with your child. Celebrate the progress they’ve made and ask them what they are excited to learn next. (Reports came home last week or at conferences) Reading Habits: Encourage 20 minutes of daily reading. Whether it’s a novel, a graphic novel, or an informational article, consistent exposure is key to maintaining those high reading percentiles. Math in the Real World: Help your child see math in action, whether it's calculating a tip, measuring ingredients for a recipe, or tracking sports statistics. IXL-Students in Grades 1-8 have access to IXL in school and at home where they can receive personalized practice and instruction in math and language arts. Thank you for your continued partnership in making St. Martha a place where academic excellence thrives!

textSections.heading: Girls Math & Science Day!
textSections.text:
The Mid-Michigan chapter of Graduate Women in Science (GWIS) would like to invite the students at your school to the 2026 Girls Math and Science Day at Michigan State University on Saturday, Mar 14th, 2026. This is a fantastic opportunity for middle school-aged students to participate in STEM demonstrations led by some of MSU's enthusiastic and knowledgeable students and researchers. Registration is FREE of cost and will be open from Feb 01st - 28th (or until spots are filled) ! This year, we want students to see and experience more types of STEM fields throughout the day, with the ability to revisit an activity as many times as they like. Therefore, the day for each participant will consist of two faculty talks, two 20-minute STEM-themed activities according to the student preference, a science fair-like session with a scavenger hunt, an afternoon snack, and an ice cream social with a gift bag giveaway and thank-you note signing. Students must register for the event using this link: https://forms.gle/Eguc9Dik8f29P8KYA
Pine Hills Boys & Girls Camp
Pine Hills Boys & Girls Camp is now preparing for its upcoming camp season, and registration opens March 1 . This popular camp is open to current 6th, 7th, and 8th graders , and spots are limited. Last year, the Girls Camp filled completely within one hour of registration opening , with many campers placed on a waitlist. Families interested in learning more about Pine Hills Camp or receiving registration information should reach out directly to Pine Hills or visit pinehillscamp .com. A “Save the Date” flyer with camp information is attached. Don’t miss the opportunity!

Lifetouch Concerns
Last week, through news reports and social media, I became aware of concerns regarding Lifetouch photography. After reading several articles and consulting with Will Bloomfield, the Diocesan attorney, we have decided to move forward with Spring Pictures through Lifetouch. The discussion centers on the ownership of Lifetouch’s parent company, Shutterfly, which is owned by the private equity firm Apollo Global Management. Leon Black, the former CEO of Apollo, has been named in publicly released Epstein-related documents. As a result, rumors circulated online suggesting that student photos were at risk of being shared. These claims are untrue. We reviewed Lifetouch’s official statement on the matter and discussed it thoroughly. Mr. Bloomfield, Father Ryan, and I are satisfied with the clarification and reassurances provided. At this time, we feel confident proceeding with Lifetouch. You have the right to opt out if you are so inclined. Thank you, Mrs. Andrea Patton

Winter NWEA test results were given to the students in an envelope. Please look for these to come home from school today. If you came to conferences last week, you have already received these envelopes with your student's scores. MATHCOUNTS is a national middle school mathematics program that builds problem-solving skills and fosters achievement through four levels of fun, in-person “bee”-style contests. We are so proud of our students for their hard work, dedication, and willingness to challenge themselves. Way to represent our school. We’re cheering you on!

textSections.heading: Lifetouch Concerns
textSections.text: Last week, through news reports and social media, I became aware of concerns regarding Lifetouch photography. After reading several articles and consulting with Will Bloomfield, the Diocesan attorney, we have decided to move forward with Spring Pictures through Lifetouch. The discussion centers on the ownership of Lifetouch’s parent company, Shutterfly, which is owned by the private equity firm Apollo Global Management. Leon Black, the former CEO of Apollo, has been named in publicly released Epstein-related documents. As a result, rumors circulated online suggesting that student photos were at risk of being shared. These claims are untrue. We reviewed Lifetouch’s official statement on the matter and discussed it thoroughly. Mr. Bloomfield, Father Ryan, and I are satisfied with the clarification and reassurances provided. At this time, we feel confident proceeding with Lifetouch. You have the right to opt out if you are so inclined. Thank you, Mrs. Andrea Patton

textSections.heading: NWEA Test Results
textSections.text: Winter NWEA test results were given to the students in an envelope. Please look for these to come home from school today. If you came to conferences last week, you have already received these envelopes with your student's scores. Please remember that these NWEA tests are just a snapshot for how your student did on that particular day. We will have one more round of testing before the end of the year.

textSections.heading: MathCounts
textSections.text: Good luck to our MathCounts Team as they head to Michigan State University this Friday for the MATHCOUNTS competition! MATHCOUNTS is a national middle school mathematics program that builds problem-solving skills and fosters achievement through four levels of fun, in-person “bee”-style contests. We are so proud of our students for their hard work, dedication, and willingness to challenge themselves. Way to represent our school. We’re cheering you on!

textSections.heading: Mrs. Burkhardt's Class Lenten Shoe Drive
textSections.text: Unfortunately, many people in Michigan can’t afford warm or new shoes. By giving your new or gently used shoes to Footprints of Michigan, these people have the opportunity to stay warm and comfortable through the winter and every season. St. Martha School will collect all kinds and sizes of shoes from flip-flops to tennis shoes and boots. Drop off will be in front of the school office throughout Lent. Thank you for your kind donations. For more info on Footprints of Michigan visit: https://www. footprintsofmichigan.org/

textSections.heading: Bake Sale at Fish Fry Fridays!
textSections.text: Join us during Fish Fry Friday nights for a bake sale featuring delicious homemade treats. Proceeds support our PSO events and help fund activities for our school community. We are also looking for volunteers to donate baked goods and to help sell items during the Friday Fish Fry events! Special Notes: Friday, February 27th , is reserved for 7th grade families , who will be fundraising to support their spring field trip . Please stop by and support their efforts! Friday, March 6th, is reserved for 8th grade families, who will be fundraising to support their trip to Mackinac Island! Please stop by and support their efforts.

Girls Math & Science Day!
The Mid-Michigan chapter of Graduate Women in Science (GWIS) would like to invite the students at your school to the 2026 Girls Math and Science Day at Michigan State University on Saturday, Mar 14th, 2026. This is a fantastic opportunity for middle school-aged students to participate in STEM demonstrations led by some of MSU's enthusiastic and knowledgeable students and researchers. Registration is FREE of cost and will be open from Feb 01st - 28th (or until spots are filled) ! This year, we want students to see and experience more types of STEM fields throughout the day, with the ability to revisit an activity as many times as they like. Therefore, the day for each participant will consist of two faculty talks, two 20-minute STEM-themed activities according to the student preference, a science fair-like session with a scavenger hunt, an afternoon snack, and an ice cream social with a gift bag giveaway and thank-you note signing. Students must register for the event using this link: https://forms.gle/Eguc9Dik8f29P8KYA
Pine Hills Boys & Girls Camp
Pine Hills Boys & Girls Camp is now preparing for its upcoming camp season, and registration opens March 1 . This popular camp is open to current 6th, 7th, and 8th graders , and spots are limited. Last year, the Girls Camp filled completely within one hour of registration opening , with many campers placed on a waitlist. Families interested in learning more about Pine Hills Camp or receiving registration information should reach out directly to Pine Hills or visit pinehillscamp .com. A “Save the Date” flyer with camp information is attached. Don’t miss the opportunity!

Stewardship for Saints and Scholars Campaign pledges surpasses $58 Million!
To all of our school families who have already participated in the S3 campaign with your generous gifts of time, talent, prayers and gifts - THANK YOU!! St. Martha will benefit greatly from your generosity: Our school families will be eligible for increased amounts of tuition assistance. Our teachers will receive signing bonuses and retention bonuses as well as additional formation and training. At St. Martha School, our campaign dollars are being used to add on 6 new classrooms in order to accommodate our current needs! Funds from this campaign will help parishes, families and teachers now and into the future as our Catholic schools continue to be ever-more on mission, affordable and accessible. If you have not participated in the campaign, now is your chance. Please prayerfully consider contributing to the campaign with your gift of time, talent, prayers and gifts. Also, please consider asking grandparents and other relatives to participate as well. Use this link to go to the campaign website where online donations can be made. Thank you, in advance; Together, we will raise up the next generation of Saints and Scholars!

textSections.heading: Girls Math & Science Day!
textSections.text:
The Mid-Michigan chapter of Graduate Women in Science (GWIS) would like to invite the students at your school to the 2026 Girls Math and Science Day at Michigan State University on Saturday, Mar 14th, 2026. This is a fantastic opportunity for middle school-aged students to participate in STEM demonstrations led by some of MSU's enthusiastic and knowledgeable students and researchers. Registration is FREE of cost and will be open from Feb 01st - 28th (or until spots are filled) ! This year, we want students to see and experience more types of STEM fields throughout the day, with the ability to revisit an activity as many times as they like. Therefore, the day for each participant will consist of two faculty talks, two 20-minute STEM-themed activities according to the student preference, a science fair-like session with a scavenger hunt, an afternoon snack, and an ice cream social with a gift bag giveaway and thank-you note signing. Students must register for the event using this link: https://forms.gle/Eguc9Dik8f29P8KYA
Pine Hills Boys & Girls Camp
Pine Hills Boys & Girls Camp is now preparing for its upcoming camp season, and registration opens March 1 . This popular camp is open to current 6th, 7th, and 8th graders , and spots are limited. Last year, the Girls Camp filled completely within one hour of registration opening , with many campers placed on a waitlist. Families interested in learning more about Pine Hills Camp or receiving registration information should reach out directly to Pine Hills or visit pinehillscamp .com. A “Save the Date” flyer with camp information is attached. Don’t miss the opportunity!

A Message from Mrs. Patton
Dear St. Martha School Community, After much prayer, reflection, and many family conversations over the past few years, I have made the decision that I will retire at the conclusion of this school year. This is something my husband and I have been thoughtfully discerning for quite a while, and while it feels like the right time, it comes with a full heart, deep gratitude, and a mixture of emotions that are difficult to put into words. I have been blessed to serve in Catholic education for 37 years, 29 of those years right here at St. Martha School. St. Martha has been more than a place of work. It has been my second home, my ministry, and a community that has shaped me in countless ways. Along the way, I have been gifted with countless friendships that I will forever treasure. These relationships have meant more to me than I can fully express. I am profoundly grateful for our incredible teachers and staff, both past and present. Working alongside such dedicated, faith-filled professionals over the past 29 years has been one of the greatest joys of my career and truthfully, one of the biggest reasons it has been so hard to say goodbye. Your commitment to our students, your passion, and your love for Catholic education inspire me every single day. I have learned so much from each of you, laughed often, been humbled regularly, and am continually amazed by the work you do. It has truly been an honor to serve with you, learn from you, and cheer you on along the way. I am especially thankful for the guidance and support of our pastors. Fr. Mike, our former pastor, played a vital role in setting a strong and faithful foundation for the future. His steady leadership, pastoral care, and commitment to Catholic education laid the groundwork upon which our school and parish continue to grow. Fr. Ryan, our current pastor, brings a dynamic and faith-filled energy that is moving St. Martha forward in powerful ways. His vision, enthusiasm, and deep love for the Lord are guiding our school and parish into a vibrant and successful future rooted firmly in faith. I am deeply grateful for how both pastors’ guidance supported me personally and strengthened St. Martha School in lasting ways. Students and families, thank you for being the heart and joy of St. Martha. Watching our students grow in faith, knowledge, and character has been one of the greatest privileges of my life. I have loved every minute spent in classrooms, popping into hallways, sharing laughs at lunch, attending school events, and hearing the wonderful (and sometimes hilarious) stories our students are so eager to tell. Being with the children and witnessing their curiosity, kindness, energy, and faith has been the very best part of my days. Our families’ trust, partnership, and commitment to this community are what make St. Martha such a truly special place, and I am endlessly grateful to you. While leaving will be a huge change and is certainly bittersweet, I am filled with confidence and hope for the future of St. Martha School. This will continue to be a strong, rigorous, and faith-filled school where children are known, loved, and challenged to be their very best. I am confident that we will find an amazing new leader, and I know that St. Martha will continue to thrive. As we enter this “next act”, my husband and I are truly looking forward to what lies ahead. We are excited to spend more time together, to visit our children in Grand Rapids and Nashville, to care for our granddogs (and someday, we hope, grandkids!), and to travel. Though I am retiring from my role, I am not leaving the St. Martha community. I will remain an active member of the parish and will assist with the transition to support our new administrator in any way I can. Thank you for the prayers, kindness, and love you have shown me throughout the years. Serving this community and the Catholic Church has been one of the greatest blessings of my life. St. Martha School will forever hold a special place in my heart. With deep gratitude, Andrea Patton

The Michigan School Vocal Music Association (MSVMA) State Honors Choir is a prestigious, competitive program that recognizes the top vocal talent across Michigan, taking students from regional recognition to advanced state-level ensembles. Congratulations to Mrs. DiMenno, director, and the following honors choir members: Olesia Mankowski, Alexandria Chesney, Ginger Obenauf, Chisom Obinwanne, and Lucia Rivet. Despite the cold and snow, they performed beautifully with the State Honors Choir at DeVos Hall last Thursday. We are incredibly proud of our talented students and deeply grateful to Mrs. DiMenno for her dedication and time in preparing them for this outstanding achievement.

Catholic Schools Week Mass-Thank you!
Thank you to everyone who attended our Catholic Schools Week Mass this past Sunday! We appreciate you braving the snow to join us. We were so proud to see our students actively participating in the liturgy as lectors, gift bearers, and altar servers. The children’s choir, accompanied by flute and violin, joyfully led the music, making this Mass a truly meaningful celebration of our Catholic mission through prayer, participation, and song. Students who wore their uniforms and attended the 10 a.m. Mass received a Free Dress Coupon for February 4th. If a student did not receive their coupon, they may stop by the office to pick one up. A special thank you to the CCW and the Knights of Columbus for preparing and hosting a delicious breakfast for our community!

Parent Teacher Conference by Teacher Request
At St. Martha School, we value strong communication and a close partnership between home and school. Our teachers regularly monitor each student’s academic progress, social development, and overall well-being and will reach out when a conference would be especially beneficial. Parent-teacher conferences will take place by teacher request. Teachers will send conference requests via email on Tuesday, February 3, and the email will include a link to sign up for a conference time. For families who are contacted, conferences will be formally scheduled on Wednesday, Feb. 11 after school and Thursday, Feb. 12 in the afternoon. The sign up will be coming soon. Please know that this process does not limit communication in any way. Parents are always welcome to reach out to teachers with questions, concerns, or to request a conversation at any time. We believe open and ongoing communication is essential to helping our students thrive. Thank you for your continued trust, support, and partnership. We are grateful to work together as a caring school community.

Hazardous Travel Conditions
Children come to school from communities of varying distances where weather conditions may differ. Even though St. Martha is open, parents who feel that driving conditions are unsafe should keep their children home until weather conditions improve. A call to the school office should be made to notify us that your child will not be in school. When weather becomes dangerous or threatening during the school day, parents who are concerned may pick up their children.
School Closing Protocol
We depend on the information provided by Local TV stations, early morning conditions and severe storm warning predictions to make the decision regarding a school closure. We understand closing for snow days can be difficult for working families, but the safety of all of our students and staff are a top priority. In the winter, we suggest following weather reports and if winter storms are predicted, to have a plan in place in case school does have to close. The school will contact school families first via text, and email. We also post on Facebook, WILX and WLNS once we have sent out communications from the school.

textSections.text: Thank you to everyone who attended our Catholic Schools Week Mass this past Sunday! We appreciate you braving the snow to join us. textSections.heading: Hazardous Travel Conditions
textSections.text:
Children come to school from communities of varying distances where weather conditions may differ. Even though St. Martha is open, parents who feel that driving conditions are unsafe should keep their children home until weather conditions improve. A call to the school office should be made to notify us that your child will not be in school. When weather becomes dangerous or threatening during the school day, parents who are concerned may pick up their children.
School Closing Protocol
We depend on the information provided by Local TV stations, early morning conditions and severe storm warning predictions to make the decision regarding a school closure. We understand closing for snow days can be difficult for working families, but the safety of all of our students and staff are a top priority. In the winter, we suggest following weather reports and if winter storms are predicted, to have a plan in place in case school does have to close. The school will contact school families first via text, and email. We also post on Facebook, WILX and WLNS once we have sent out communications from the school.

Fleece & Thank you Project
As part of our Catholic Schools Week celebrations, our students will be participating in a meaningful service project rooted in compassion and service to others. During the week, students will gather with their Houses to make fleece blankets through the organization Fleece & Thank You . This wonderful nonprofit has a mission to provide every child facing hospital treatments with a colorful, comforting fleece blanket, along with a video message of encouragement from the blanket’s maker. We are seeking parent donors who are willing to contribute $30 to sponsor one blanket kit. Your purchase of our blanket kits helps cover the entire process of blanket delivery from raw materials to hospital bed. Our goal is to make 11 blankets total. Each House will make two blankets, and our Preschool students will make one blanket together. The school will order all blanket kits directly through Fleece & Thank You. If you choose to donate toward a blanket, please click the link below to sign up. Mrs. Farnsworth will send you the link to make the donation online through Parish Giving. This project is a beautiful way for our students to live out our faith by serving others with kindness and love. Thank you for considering supporting this special Catholic Schools Week activity. Go to https://fleeceandthankyou.org/ to read more about this project. Sign up to donate $30 for the cost of one blanket kit. There are a few spots available to donate so we can cover the cost of shipping. Once you sign up, Mrs. Farnsworth will send you a link for payment.

The Knights of Columbus Free Throw Championship is sponsored annually, with winners progressing through local, district, and jurisdictional competitions. Parents must drop students off at the gym and sign a form in order to participate.

Parent Teacher Conference by Teacher Request
At St. Martha School, we value strong communication and a close partnership between home and school. Our teachers regularly monitor each student’s academic progress, social development, and overall well-being and will reach out when a conference would be especially beneficial. Parent-teacher conferences will take place by teacher request. Teachers will send conference requests via email on Tuesday, February 3, and the email will include a link to sign up for a conference time. Please know that this process does not limit communication in any way. Parents are always welcome to reach out to teachers with questions, concerns, or to request a conversation at any time. We believe open and ongoing communication is essential to helping our students thrive. Thank you for your continued trust, support, and partnership. We are grateful to work together as a caring school community. Parent-Teacher Conferences: Frequently Asked Questions Why are conferences held by teacher request only? Our teachers continuously assess each student’s academic progress, social development, and overall well-being. Conferences are scheduled when a conversation would be especially helpful and meaningful in supporting your child’s growth. Does this mean my child is struggling if I’m contacted? Not at all. textSections.heading: Hazardous Travel Conditions
textSections.text:
Children come to school from communities of varying distances where weather conditions may differ. Even though St. Martha is open, parents who feel that driving conditions are unsafe should keep their children home until weather conditions improve. A call to the school office should be made to notify us that your child will not be in school. When weather becomes dangerous or threatening during the school day, parents who are concerned may pick up their children.
School Closing Protocol
We depend on the information provided by Local TV stations, early morning conditions and severe storm warning predictions to make the decision regarding a school closure. We understand closing for snow days can be difficult for working families, but the safety of all of our students and staff are a top priority. In the winter, we suggest following weather reports and if winter storms are predicted, to have a plan in place in case school does have to close. The school will contact school families first via text, and email. We also post on Facebook, WILX and WLNS once we have sent out communications from the school.

textSections.heading: Fleece & Thank you Project
textSections.text:
As part of our Catholic Schools Week celebrations, our students will be participating in a meaningful service project rooted in compassion and service to others. During the week, students will gather with their Houses to make fleece blankets through the organization Fleece & Thank You . This wonderful nonprofit has a mission to provide every child facing hospital treatments with a colorful, comforting fleece blanket, along with a video message of encouragement from the blanket’s maker. We are seeking parent donors who are willing to contribute $30 to sponsor one blanket kit. Your purchase of our blanket kits helps cover the entire process of blanket delivery from raw materials to hospital bed. Our goal is to make 11 blankets total. Each House will make two blankets, and our Preschool students will make one blanket together. The school will order all blanket kits directly through Fleece & Thank You. If you choose to donate toward a blanket, please click the link below to sign up. Mrs. Farnsworth will send you the link to make the donation online through Parish Giving. This project is a beautiful way for our students to live out our faith by serving others with kindness and love. Thank you for considering supporting this special Catholic Schools Week activity. Go to https://fleeceandthankyou.org/ to read more about this project. Sign up to donate $30 for the cost of one blanket kit. There are a few spots available to donate so we can cover the cost of shipping. Once you sign up, Mrs. Farnsworth will send you a link for payment.
Blanket Donation Sign Up

textSections.heading: Parent Teacher Conference by Teacher Request
textSections.text: At St. Martha School, we value strong communication and a close partnership between home and school. Our teachers regularly monitor each student’s academic progress, social development, and overall well-being and will reach out when a conference would be especially beneficial. Parent-teacher conferences will take place by teacher request. Teachers will send conference requests via email on Tuesday, February 3, and the email will include a link to sign up for a conference time. For families who are contacted, conferences will be formally scheduled on Wednesday, Feb. 11 after school and Thursday, Feb. 12 in the afternoon. The sign up will be coming soon. Please know that this process does not limit communication in any way. Parents are always welcome to reach out to teachers with questions, concerns, or to request a conversation at any time. We believe open and ongoing communication is essential to helping our students thrive. Thank you for your continued trust, support, and partnership. We are grateful to work together as a caring school community. Parent-Teacher Conferences: Frequently Asked Questions Why are conferences held by teacher request only? Our teachers continuously assess each student’s academic progress, social development, and overall well-being. Conferences are scheduled when a conversation would be especially helpful and meaningful in supporting your child’s growth. Does this mean my child is struggling if I’m contacted? Not at all. A conference may be requested to discuss progress, strengths, learning strategies, or ways to continue supporting your child’s success. What if I am not contacted but still have questions? Parents are always encouraged to reach out to teachers at any time. Not being scheduled for a formal conference does not limit communication in any way. Can I request a conference if I feel one would be helpful? Yes. We value our partnership with families and welcome parent communication whenever questions or concerns arise. Our goal is to ensure that all conversations between parents and teachers are thoughtful, timely, and focused on what is best for each child.

If you choose to donate toward a blanket, please click the link below to sign up. Mrs. Farnsworth will send you the link to make the donation online through Parish Giving. Parent Teacher Conference by Teacher Request
At St. Martha School, we value strong communication and a close partnership between home and school. Our teachers regularly monitor each student’s academic progress, social development, and overall well-being and will reach out when a conference would be especially beneficial. Parent-teacher conferences will take place by teacher request. Teachers will send conference requests via email on Tuesday, February 3, and the email will include a link to sign up for a conference time. For families who are contacted, conferences will be formally scheduled on Wednesday, Feb. 11 after school and Thursday, Feb. 12 in the afternoon. The sign up will be coming soon. Please know that this process does not limit communication in any way. Parents are always welcome to reach out to teachers with questions, concerns, or to request a conversation at any time. We believe open and ongoing communication is essential to helping our students thrive. Thank you for your continued trust, support, and partnership. We are grateful to work together as a caring school community. Parent-Teacher Conferences: Frequently Asked Questions Why are conferences held by teacher request only? Our teachers continuously assess each student’s academic progress, social development, and overall well-being. Conferences are scheduled when a conversation would be especially helpful and meaningful in supporting your child’s growth. Does this mean my child is struggling if I’m contacted? Not at all. A conference may be requested to discuss progress, strengths, learning strategies, or ways to continue supporting your child’s success. What if I am not contacted but still have questions? Parents are always encouraged to reach out to teachers at any time. Not being scheduled for a formal conference does not limit communication in any way. Can I request a conference if I feel one would be helpful? Yes. We value our partnership with families and welcome parent communication whenever questions or concerns arise. Our goal is to ensure that all conversations between parents and teachers are thoughtful, timely, and focused on what is best for each child.
